profile.npc_static_bio: Nymphs are the immature stage of giant mantises with underdeveloped forelimbs and softer chitin than adults. They rely on ambush tactics and swarm coordination to bring down prey larger than themselves, striking repeatedly with weak venom. Their compound eyes detect motion with exceptional sensitivity, though depth perception remains poor until maturity. Solitary nymphs fall easy prey to larger predators, so they instinctively cluster near adults for protection.
